Synthetic Methods
EnantioselectiveA llenation of Terminal Alkynes Catalyzed by Copper
Halides of Mixed Oxidation States and Its Application to the Total
Synthesis of Scorodonin
Guolin Wu+,Y uan Yao+,G en Li, Xue Zhang,* Hui Qian,* and Shengming Ma*
Dedicated to Professor E. Peter Kgndig on the occasion of his 75th birthday
Abstract: Naturally occurring conjugated allenynes are of
general interest owing to their potent and various biological
activities.T he 1,5-H transfer of alka-1,4-diyn-3-yl amines
would be one of the most straightforwardy et challenging
approaches to such compounds since,i np rinciple,t wo
regioisomers may be formed involving two C@Ct riple bonds.
Herein, ac atalytic recipe of copper halides with mixed
oxidation states,i .e., CuCl/CuBr2,h as been identified to
address the issues of the side reaction of conjugate addition
and the selectivity of 1,5-H transfer of alka-1,4-diyn-3-yl
amines in EATA (enantioselective allenation of terminal
alkynes) reaction involving 2-alkynals.T his method provided
various allenynes with excellent enantioselectivities,a nd was
also applied to the first highly enantioselective total synthesis of
natural product scorodonin. Mechanistic studies and DFT
calculations elucidated the regioselectivity for the observed 1,5-
Ht ransfer.
Introduction
Allenes exist in over 150 natural products[1] and are av ery
important class of basic chemicals for organic synthesis,[2]
pharmaceuticals,[1b] and materials science.[3] Of particular
interest, the conjugated allenynes are one of the most
conspicuous structural unit in these natural products (Fig-
ure 1A )[1b,4 ] and highlight the potential utility in organic
synthesis.[5] However,t he lack of an efficient and flexible
synthesis has prevented its further synthetic applications and
biological studies.M uch efforts have been devoted over the
past few decades to develop new methods for the efficient
synthesis of allenes.[6,7 ] In particular,t he allenation of
terminal alkynes (ATA)r eaction promoted with transition
metals,s uch as Cu,[8] Zn,[9] Au,[10] has received great attention
(Figure 1B ). However,s uch reactions with 2-alkynals are still
problematic and have never been reported since there are
several challenges to be solved:( 1) the potential conjugate
addition of amines with 2-alkynals;( 2) the site-selectivity of
1,5-H transfer[11,1 2] within the 1,4-alkadiyn-3-yl amines (Int)
bearing two different C@Ct riple bonds;( 3) the suitable
catalyst to initiate the reaction with good efficiency and
enantiocontrol. Here we have identified ac atalytic recipe of
copper halides with mixed oxidation states to address such
selectivity issues on the EATA reaction of 2-alkynals and
terminal alkynes in the presence of the commercially
available (S)- or (R)-a,a-diphenylprolinol (Figure 1C ). Re-
markably,t his new recipe is highlighted by the first highly
enantioselective concise total synthesis of both enantiomers
of scorodonin.
Results and Discussion

reaction of 3-t-butyldimethylsilylpropynal 1a and tertiary
propargylic alcohol 2a in the presence of (S)-a,a-diphenyl-

Synthetic applications of these chiral allenynes were
demonstrated as shown in Figure 2C :t he reaction may be
easily scaled up to 10 mmol, affording allenyne (Ra)-4b k with
99 % ee. TheM itsunobu reaction of (Ra)-4b k with phthali-
mide proceeded smoothly to afford (Ra)-7 in 70 %y ield with
98 % ee. This primary allenol could also be easily transformed
to the corresponding ester (Ra)-8 without racemization. In
addition, the triazole-tethered allenes (Ra)-9 could be suc-
cessfully assembled in high ee via desilylation followed by
cycloaddition with azide (see details in Supporting Informa-
tion).[13]
Scorodonin, ab iologically active metabolite isolated from
submerged cultures of the mushroom Marasmius scorodo-
nius,s howed interesting antibacterial and antifungal activi-
ties.[4d] Due to the presence of the highly sensitive conjugate
allenyne unit, its highly enantioselective synthesis is challeng-
ing and has not been realized.[14] We reasoned that the EATA
reaction of 2-alkynals would be as traightforward approach to
the projected compound. As shown in Figure 2D -i, our
synthesis commenced with the EATA reaction of 2-alkynal
1b with propargyl alcohol 2c ,w hich easily furnished allenyne
(Ra)-4b c on ag ram scale with 98 % ee. Subsequent desilyla-
tion and TBS protection delivered enantioenriched (Ra)-10 in
75 %y ield over two steps.N ext, the hydroxymethylation of
terminal allenyne (Ra)-10 proved to be unexpectedly chal-
lenging, with the commonly used base/paraformaldehyde
conditions failing to realize this transformation (see details in
Supporting Information). Ultimately,a modified alkynylation
of (Ra)-10 with paraformaldehyde in the presence of Zn-
(OTf)2/TMEDA/Et3Ns uccessfully generated (Ra)-11 in 65 %
yield with 94 % ee.[15] Finally,a nA ppel chlorination[16] of the
hydroxyl group with NCS,f ollowed by acid-mediated desily-
lation afforded (@)-scorodonin with 94 % ee. Likewise,t he
synthesis of (++)-scorodonin was executed following the same
synthetic route just by replacing (S)-3 with (R)-3 in the step of
EATA reaction with as imilar yield and enantioselectivity
(Figure 2D -ii, see details in Supporting Information).
To gain insight into the reaction mechanism, as eries of

> 99 % ee,c onfirming that (R,S)-5b a was the key intermedi-
ate.I nterestingly,t he use of CuBr2 alone afforded the product

CuCl was added, (Ra)-4b a was afforded in 14 %y ield with

ure 3B -b). Thes ame results were observed for the reaction of
3-TMS-2-alkynal 1b with TBS-acetylene 2m (Figure 3B -c).
Thus,i ts eems that the silyl-substituted terminal alkynes
cannot be converted to the corresponding allenes.T of urther
investigate the role of the silyl group in the starting alkynal,
as terically smaller phenethyl group was applied instead of the
bulky trialkylsilyl moiety in the aldehyde (Figure 3B -d).
Interestingly,t he allenyne product (Ra)-4d a was obtained,
albeit in 14 %y ield with 98 % ee together with 17 %y ield of
the 1,4-diyn-3-yl amine intermediate (S,S)-5d a remaining.
WhatQsm ore,t he reaction of 2-alkynal 1c and propargylic
alcohol 2a ,i nt he presence of (S)-3,o r 1e and 2n in the
presence of (R)-3,w hich both have the same substituent on
the Csp atom afforded the allene (Ra)-4c a or (Sa)-4e n with an
excellent ee (Figure 3B -(e,f)). Theh igh ee was maintained
when 1,4-diyn-3-yl amine intermediates (S,S)-5d a and (S)-5c a
as well as (R)-5e n were treated under the standard conditions.
All these results suggested that (1) 2-alkynals are NOT
limited to the 3-silyl substituted ones,( 2) the high regiose-
lectivity of this EATA reaction is not dominated by the steric
effect of the 3-substituent in the conjugated 2-alkynals,a nd
(3) only one triple bond in (S)-5c a as well as (R)-5e n
underwent the 1,5-H transfer and b-N-elimination to form the
allene unit.

In order to further rationalize the observed unique regio-
and enantio-selectivity,D FT calculations were carried out to

Thec alculation starts from (R,S)-5b a-CuBr2 complex Int1

moiety that is in possible positions for the 1,5-H transfer.
Thus,s ix transition structures are located for the competing
regioselective 1,5-H transfer,w hich are denoted as TS1_a–c
and TS1_a’’–c’’,s eparately (Figure 4a ). Thei somerization of

formation of the 1,5-H transfer precursors Int2_a’’–c’’ (path b,
Figure 4a ). Thes ubsequent 1,5-H transfer is realized via six-

Among the six transition structures, TS1_a,w hich is referring
to the 1,5-H transfer of the methylene hydrogen (Ha)t ot he
hydroxyalkyl-substituted triple bond, is found to be the most
favorable one,d ue to the lowest free energy barrier of
25.0 kcal mol@1.T he results could interpret the formation of
the highly regioselective of product allenyne (Ra)-4b a via the
1,5-H transfer to the hydroxyalkyl-substituted triple bond in
the experiment (No regioisomer (Sa)-6b a was observed,
Figure 3A ). Moreover,t he fact that the methylene hydrogen
in (S)-diphenylprolinol moiety participates in the 1,5-H
transfer is in agreement with the deuterium-labeling experi-
ment in our previous work.[8c]
To investigate the origin of the regioselectivity,n atural

Conclusion
In conclusion, we have developed ah ighly efficient CuCl/
CuBr2 co-catalyzed enantioselective allenation (EATA)r e-
action of 2-alkynals by using the commercially available (S)-
or (R)-a,a-diphenylprolinol involving the highly regio- and
stereo-selective 1,5-H transfer of 1,4-diyn-3-yl amine inter-
mediates.T his method could tolerate aw ide range of
functional groups including the chiral secondary free prop-
argylic alcohols,a nd provides as eries of allenynes with
excellent enantioselectivities (up to > 99 % ee). Thee nan-
tioenriched allenynes can be readily transformed into various
building blocks.T his protocol has been successfully applied to
the first highly enantioselective total synthesis of linear allenic
natural product (@)-scorodonin and its enantiomer.F urther
mechanistic studies involving both experiments and DFT
calculations revealed that the configuration of proline is
responsible for the stereo- and regioselectivity observed in
this transformation.
